title: Clone a disk to another disk
summary: Use `dd` to copy the entire contents of one disk to another. This is useful for migrating data or creating an exact copy of a drive.
prerequisites: Destination disk connected and larger than or equal to the source disk
Knowledge of both disk device identifiers

steps.explain: Copy the source disk to the destination disk using a 4MB block size. Replace <SOURCE_DRIVE> and <DEST_DRIVE> with the correct device identifiers (e.g., /dev/disk2 and /dev/disk3). This erases the destination drive.
steps.cmd: sudo dd bs=4m conv=noerror if=<SOURCE_DRIVE> of=<DEST_DRIVE> status=progress

placeholders.name: SOURCE_DRIVE
placeholders.description: Device identifier of the source disk

placeholders.name: DEST_DRIVE
placeholders.description: Device identifier of the destination disk

steps.expect: Progress information will be displayed as the disk is cloned.

warnings: This command will completely erase all data on the destination drive.
Ensure the destination drive is at least as large as the source drive.
Verify device identifiers carefully to avoid data loss.

rollback.explain: There is no direct rollback for `dd`. The destination drive's original data is lost.
